The bridge at night was a different creature than the bridge by day. Daylight made it functional, ordinary, a mere conveyance of steel and concrete. But darkness transformed it into something luminous and suspended, a necklace of light draped across the throat of the river. He walked across it slowly, savoring the peculiar solitude of being between two places, belonging to neither. The water below was black and unknowable, a mirror that reflected only the city's vanity... its towers, its ambitions, its trembling constellations of electric light. Cars passed him like bright-eyed animals, their headlights sweeping the railings. He stopped at the center. The wind carried salt and diesel and something older, something oceanic and indifferent. He leaned against the railing and felt the bridge hum beneath him, a low vibration... the frequency of purpose, of engineered intention. Even steel, he thought, can learn to sing if you stretch it far enough between two fixed points of longing.
